record.what_it_does: ByteDance's international workplace suite: chat, docs, calendar, base, approvals, and a developer open platform.
record.auth_notes: Each app has an App ID and App Secret, exchanged for short-lived bearer tokens. A tenant_access_token acts as the app, and an app_access_token exists for both custom apps and store apps. A user_access_token acts as a user and comes from a standard OAuth 2.0 authorization-code flow. The authorize endpoint is https://accounts.larksuite.com/open-apis/authen/v1/authorize, and you must request the offline_access scope to receive a refresh_token. A multi-user agent toolkit would use OAuth2 user_access_token plus refresh_token. Bots would use tenant_access_token. I found no static personal access token or plain API key. The App Secret is never sent as an API key on its own, so I dropped api_key. I did not see the token-exchange endpoint URL on any fetched page.
record.access_notes: A developer can create a free Lark tenant (Starter plan, $0, up to 20 users per third-party pricing summaries) and a custom app (企业自建应用). The tenant admin approves the custom app's scopes, and in your own tenant that admin is you. So working credentials for development and single-tenant use are self-serve. Distributing to other tenants requires a store app (商店应用). That means a Lark Open Platform listing review, plus each tenant admin's review at install time. Per-plan OpenAPI call quotas are unconfirmed: a third-party blog says Starter gets 10,000 API calls per month, but the official plans page did not render for me.
record.api_breadth_notes: REST APIs under /open-apis cover IM and messaging, contacts, calendar, docs, drive, base (bitable), sheets, wiki, approval, mail, VC, tasks, HR and more. That is hundreds of endpoints, though I did not count them exactly. Official SDKs exist for Go, Node, Java and Python. The WebSocket long connection is for event delivery.
record.mcp_notes: The npm package is @larksuiteoapi/lark-mcp (github.com/larksuite/lark-openapi-mcp). It is in Beta and self-hosted, using stdio or SSE/HTTP. The --domain flag targets Lark international, and OAuth with --token-mode user_access_token is supported. Neither the repo nor searches showed a Lark-hosted remote MCP URL.
record.blocker_notes: The API is public, and creating a custom app on a free tenant is self-serve. A single OAuth app serving many external tenants must be published as a store app. That requires a Lark Open Platform listing review, and each tenant admin must also approve the install and its scopes. Lark international (open.larksuite.com) and Feishu (open.feishu.cn) are separate platforms with separate domains.
